WoW: Forever

Druid

Druid is four roles on one character, and Forever changed a gearing rule outright: your weapon's damage now scales Bear and Cat form. In Classic it did not matter at all.

WoW: Forever · Updated November 13, 2026 · Client build 1.60.1.70938 · Null Ossuary

A guide to the live game, 1 to 60. Numbers are the client's at build 1.60.1.70938 with Blizzard's hotfixes through November 12. Talent builds on the spec pages are Icy Veins' and Wowhead's, named and dated; both sites now publish orders from 10 to 60 and level 60 builds. Rotation advice past 40 also draws on WoWSims, which is a model, and on combat logs it has fitted. No raid is open until December 9, so no page here rests on a raid log. The Feral talent older guides call Mangle is Primal BitePrimal BiteTalent · Rank 1 of 3CastInstantCost20 RageRangeMeleeCooldown6 sec cooldownBite the target, dealing 100% normal damage plus 42 and generating a high amount of threat.. If a tooltip differs from the text, go by the text.

Bear and Cat share one tree and one levelling build, but they get separate pages: the rotations, stat priorities and gear are different. Bear is your only combat form from 10 to 20. Aquatic FormAquatic FormLevel 16 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCost20% of base ManaDurationUntil cancelledShapeshift into Aquatic Form, increasing swim speed by 50% and allowing the druid to breathe underwater. Also protects the caster from Polymorph effects. The act of shapeshifting frees the caster of Polymorph and Movement Impairing effects. arrives at 16 and is for swimming. Cat Form does not exist until 20, and it comes from a quest chain in Moonglade rather than a trainer. See the Feral — Cat page for the chain.

You do not have to level in the spec you will play. Both guide sites say to level Feral or Balance and heal dungeons in that build. From 40 your class trainer sells Dual Specialization for 50 gold, per Wowhead.

Two habits from Classic you must unlearn. First, your weapon's damage counts in Bear and Cat Form, so pick the weapon for its DPS. Second, the Cat energy trick is gone: FurorFurorTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantGives you a 100% chance to gain 10 Rage when shapeshifting into Bear Form or Dire Bear Form. Shapeshifting into Cat Form restores 100% of the Energy you had when last in Cat Form, plus 10 Energy per second spent outside Bear Form or Dire Bear Form, up to 100 Energy. no longer hands you a flat 40 Energy for entering Cat Form. At 5/5 it restores the Energy you last had plus 10 per second spent outside Bear and Dire Bear Form, capped at 100, so shifting out and back cannot beat staying in Cat. The replacement is Shifting PowerShifting PowerTalentCastInstantCost55% of base ManaCooldown8 sec cooldown at 40, which turns Mana into Energy. The Bear half is unchanged: 10 rage on every shift into Bear at 5/5.

Is Druid for you?

Play Druid if you want one character that can do any job in the game, and you accept a slow first twenty levels. You have no combat form at all until Bear Form at 10, and no Cat Form until 20.

Blizzard's own class deep dive sharpens that trade-off. Druids have the "ability to serve any combat role, given the right equipment and talents," but "that versatility comes at the cost of non-damage utility." They "cannot snare targets, cannot Silence or Interrupt, and have weaker and less reliable crowd control," and their healing "relies on healing-over-time (HoT) spells that require more planning." They "lack the extended utility toolkits found on Rogues, Warriors, or Mages," so they "can perform any role but will need to rely on others to provide the complete toolkit needed for raids and dungeons."

Strengths

  • Blizzard credits Druids with the "ability to serve any combat role" — and Bear and Cat need no respec between them
  • Travel FormTravel FormLevel 30 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCost20% of base ManaDurationUntil cancelledShapeshift into Travel Form, increasing movement speed by 40%. Also protects the caster from Polymorph effects. Only useable outdoors. The act of shapeshifting frees the caster of Polymorph and Movement Impairing effects. at 30 is +40% speed outdoors, ten levels before a mount
  • Shapeshifting breaks roots and slows

Weaknesses

  • Wowhead on the early levels: "Leveling as a Feral Druid can start off feeling very slow"
  • Three separate resources, and shifting costs Mana every time
  • Blizzard: the versatility "comes at the cost of non-damage utility" — no snare, Silence or Interrupt

New to this class?

Is the rotation simple? Yes, within a form: a level-20 Cat is three buttons. You have several forms.

Is it forgiving? Bear Form multiplies your gear's armour and you can drop form to heal yourself; Cat has neither.

What carries you while levelling? Bear Form from a class quest at 10 and Cat Form at 20. In Forever your weapon's damage scales both.

Does it need a group? No. But a Feral Druid in a group will be asked to tank, and any Druid can heal a levelling dungeon.

Quality of life

  • Take the highest-DPS weapon you can get and keep sharpening stones on it. This reverses the Classic rule. Weapon speed does not matter: forms swing at a fixed speed.
  • Bear Form at 10 comes from a class quest. Go to your trainer the moment you hit 10. Until then you are a caster in cloth: Snupy spams WrathWrathLevel 1 · Spell · Nature · Rank 1 of 8Cast1.5 sec castCost10 ManaRange30 yd rangeCauses 15 to 17 Nature damage to the target. and uses MoonfireMoonfireLevel 4 · Spell · Arcane · Rank 1 of 10CastInstantCost25 ManaRange30 yd rangeDuration9 secBurns the enemy for 10 to 12 Arcane damage and then an additional 12 Arcane damage over 9 sec., trained at 4, to tag mobs first.
  • Travel FormTravel FormLevel 30 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCost20% of base ManaDurationUntil cancelledShapeshift into Travel Form, increasing movement speed by 40%. Also protects the caster from Polymorph effects. Only useable outdoors. The act of shapeshifting frees the caster of Polymorph and Movement Impairing effects. at 30 is your mount ten levels early. Instant, outdoors only, and most world objects can be used without dropping it.
  • Consumables work while shapeshifted, so a bear can drink a potion and a cat can use a Thistle Tea, per Blizzard's own list. Weapon enchants and procs fire in form too, and most doors and world objects open without dropping your shapeshift. The holdouts are most Engineering bombs, with the SAF-T and EZ-Thro recipes as the stated exceptions, and Mining and Fishing, per Icy Veins.
  • Dual Specialization is 50 gold at 40, from your class trainer, per Wowhead. That is the same level as your mount, so you may have to choose which comes first. Respec costs rise each time you pay them.
  • Spell Power is worth wearing before 20. Wowhead: it helps your spells before the forms arrive, and ThornsThornsLevel 6 · Spell · Nature · Rank 1 of 6CastInstantCost35 ManaRange30 yd rangeDuration600 secThorns sprout from the friendly target causing 3 Nature damage to attackers when hit. Lasts 600 sec. scales with it.

At level 60

Every spec has a published level 60 build now, from Icy Veins, Wowhead and, for Balance and Feral, WoWSims. They are on the spec pages with their dates. All of them reach outside their own tree: Feral and Balance take NaturalistNaturalistTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantReduces the cast time of your Healing Touch and Wild Growth spells by 0.5 sec and increases all damage you deal by 10%. for +10% damage, and Restoration takes Nature's SplendorNature's SplendorTalentCastInstantIncreases the duration of your Moonfire and Rejuvenation spells by 3 sec, your Regrowth spell by 6 sec, and your Insect Swarm spell by 2 sec. from Balance.

Dungeons. Both sites expect a Feral Druid to tank, call Cat's lack of area damage its weak point, and describe dungeon healing as light enough to add damage between heals.

Raids open December 9: Barrow Deeps for 10, Hyjal Summit for 20 and Onyxia's Lair for 40. Until then nobody has a raid log. For bear tanking, both sites aim for 440 Defense to stop boss critical strikes and say that figure is untested; Icy Veins adds that a bear cannot avoid Crushing Blows, so armour and health have to absorb them. The tier lists on both sites were written before launch and before six rounds of hotfixes.

Sources

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Where Blizzard has published an official class deep dive, that post outranks all three and the page is written from it. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools. Where the guides disagree with each other, this page says which said what.
